chapter_title: Concerning the Eighteen Great Thrones of all the Fathers
chapter_note: This chapter is largely a systematic, numbered cosmological catalogue (thrones across aeons/ships/firmaments), characteristic of the older teaching layer. A later compiler has wrapped it with a dialogue opening (¶1) and appended/extended the sequence with ecclesial-apostolic identification (¶17) and summary/doxological material (¶11–12, ¶18). One paragraph (¶10) shows a pivot from cosmic identification to institutional reference (“churches”), suggesting editorial application grafted onto a core throne-item.

paragraphs.core_text: Eighteen [great thrones for all the fathers] exist and are appointed, which are established in eighteen places! While there are nine among them [appointed in] the outer aeons, they exist [i]n all the worlds of the damage.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he speaks to his disciples:” (hagiographic container formula).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core catalogue statement is impersonal and structural (numerical scheme + aeons/worlds); the opening speech-to-disciples formula is a later compiling frame.

paragraphs.core_text: The first throne is the throne of the Father, the God of [trut]h, the King of the aeons of greatness, the one who exists; who is established [...] he alone, in his own essen[c]e, [...] apart. This is the first throne [...] the one that surpasses all the thrones.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered, impersonal throne-listing with standard Manichaean divine titles; no citation, exhortation, or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.82⟩ The second throne is that of the [gl]orious Mother of Life. She is the origin of all the emanations that have come to this world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic emanational cosmology (Mother of Life as source of emanations) in catalogue form; stylistically consistent with core teaching lists.

paragraphs.core_text: The third throne is constructed for the father, the First Man. He is the one who humiliated the entire first enmity, which existed in the worlds of darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic mythic-cosmological role statement (First Man vs. enmity/Darkness worlds) presented as part of a numbered structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth throne is that of the Beloved of the Lights, the great honoured Beloved of the aeons of greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Throne-item within the enumerated cosmic hierarchy; “Beloved of the Lights” functions as a personified cosmological figure/title within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth throne is that of the glorious Great Builder; the great architect who built the new aeon for a newness, for [a ...] for [the] fathers of light; also for a place of binding and a prison for the enemy and his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic mechanics and architecture (new aeon; prison/binding of enemy powers) stated as ontology/function, not exhortation or church regulation.

paragraphs.core_text: [The sixth thro]n[e] is that of the Living Spirit, the [glorious] mighty one, he who bore up the First Man out from the [land of darkness]; who also set in order and constructed the world [s ...] both for a cleansing of the light, [and] for a binding [of the] powers of the enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological function (rescue + world-construction for purification/binding) in the same enumerative register.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh th[rone is] that of the Third Ambassador, the king of the zone, also the master of all advices.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Catalogue identification of a named cosmological being with titles internal to the cosmic administration (“zone”, “advices”).

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth throne is that of Jesus the Splendour, who [is] the releaser and redeemer [of] all souls.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite “Jesus” vocabulary, this is a standard Manichaean cosmic hypostasis (“Jesus the Splendour”) presented as a throne-item without Gospel citation formulas; thus it reads as internal cosmology rather than NT overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: The ninth throne is the throne of the great M[ind ...]; and all the [life] that will be purified from the world returns to him.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional/application clause identifying an ecclesial referent: “he to whom] all the churches shall gather” (cosmos → contemporary institution mapping).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens as a normal throne-item within the cosmic list (“great Mind”); then pivots to institutional reach (“churches”), which breaks the cosmos→cosmos register and suggests editorial application.
Summary + doxological cadence (“for ever and ever, amen”) characteristic of editorial closure rather than core catalogue items.
Editorial transition marker (“In contrast… other nine”) functioning as structural stitching between two sub-lists.

paragraphs.core_text: Three thrones in the ship of [the d]ay: one is that of the Ambassador, the second i[s that of] the Great Spirit, the third is that of the Living Spirit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic triadic sub-structure located in a cosmic vehicle (“ship of the day”); pure internal mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.83⟩ Once again, there are another three in the ship that [belongs to the night]: the first is the throne of Jesus the Splendour, [the second is that of] the First Man, the third is tha[t of the Virgin of] Light. These six thrones are established in the two ships.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Parallel triad in the complementary cosmic ship; “Once again” here is iterative catalogue rhetoric, not a disciple-speech frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the seventh throne is established in the seventh firmament. The great King of Honour sits upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic geography (“seventh firmament”) + enthroned divine title; continues the internal cosmic placement scheme.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth throne is established in the atmosphere. The Judge of truth sits upon it, he who judges all mankind. Three paths shall be distinguished before him: one to death, one to life, on[e] to the mingling.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological-cosmological mechanics (judgment + three destinies including “mingling”) expressed as system-description, not moral exhortation.

Institutional/hagiographic identification (“apostle in the holy church… has come to you at this time”) is a classic editorial self-location of the compiler’s present and not part of the timeless cosmic catalogue.
Fragmentary concluding summary of the nine thrones ‘in this world’; functions as closing stitching rather than a fresh cosmological item, and appears in the drifted second-half register.
